corrections.issue: Attributes the Sharpe implication to Niels; Niels only says the fund's volatility reached about 90% because of static sizing. The inference that 90% vol implies an expected Sharpe of 0.9 (about twice a realistic 0.5) is Carver's, from Kelly sizing.
corrections.fix: Niels: a well-known trend manager using static position sizing saw fund volatility reach about 90% at times. Carver: under Kelly sizing that implies an expected Sharpe of 0.9 or more, about twice a realistic 0.5.

corrections.issue: Says differences are small between both sizing adjustments; Carver says the differences are not massive but that pyramiding (scaling position with forecast strength) has a much bigger effect than volatility adjustment.
corrections.fix: Position sizing studies (Saratini and Quantica) find that both volatility-adjusting positions during a trade and scaling with forecast strength help over a long backtest; differences are not large, but scaling with forecast strength (pyramiding) has the bigger effect.

completeness_estimate: 0.94 - first reader captured essentially all of Carver's methods and numbers; missed Black-Litterman, the luck caveat on manager dispersion, analyst optimism bias and the risk-premium argument, plus two small attribution/emphasis errors.
